note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Postpartum woman (4 weeks s/p C-section) with acute-onset shortness of breath at rest for ~1 hour and new nonproductive cough; advised urgent hospital evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath while sitting and watching TV.
- Timeline:
  - SOB began ~1 hour prior to call; occurred at rest.
  - New cough started yesterday; nonproductive.
  - No prior similar episodes reported.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Palpitations (“heart really going”).
  - Chest soreness with deep inspiration.
  - No chest pain at rest.
  - Feeling stressed.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Deep inspiration causes chest soreness.
  - No alleviating factors reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No sputum production.
- Obstetric/postoperative context:
  - Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
  - Baby well; no cough/cold symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Cesarean section (4 weeks postpartum).
- Otherwise denies other medical problems.
- No documented postoperative complications.

Medications:
- Codeine used regularly post-op; none taken for ~1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Advised to avoid codeine for now.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (reaction not specified).

Social History:
- At home with baby; partner at work.
- Other social factors (tobacco/alcohol/substances/occupation) not recorded.

Family History:
- Mother had leg clots (DVT).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Patient counted 30 pulse beats over an unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as slightly tachycardic.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute dyspnea in a 4-weeks postpartum patient after C-section with pleuritic-type chest soreness and perceived tachycardia. High concern for pulmonary embolism; alternative considerations include viral respiratory illness and anxiety-related symptoms.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Pulmonary embolism (PE): Strongly supported by postpartum status post C-section, abrupt SOB at rest, pleuritic soreness, and perceived tachycardia; no leg symptoms reported.
  - Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis: New cough since yesterday supports; abrupt severe dyspnea at rest is less typical.
  - Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea: Reports stress and palpitations; does not fully explain pleuritic soreness or postpartum VTE risk.

- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath, 4 weeks postpartum (possible PE)
  - Plan:
    - Immediate hospital evaluation recommended.
    - Discussed transport options (ambulance vs self-transport); patient opted to self-transport promptly.
    - Take necessary items for baby.
    - Rationale discussed: need to assess for blood clots (lungs/legs) and treat if confirmed.

- Issue 2: New nonproductive cough
  - Plan:
    - To be evaluated in hospital in context of acute SOB and postpartum risk.

- Issue 3: Palpitations/tachycardia (subjective; slight tachycardia per pulse count)
  - Plan:
    - No on-call treatment initiated; included in reason for urgent hospital assessment.

- General plan items:
  - Avoid codeine for now.
  - Proceed to hospital promptly.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full vitals (BP, respiratory rate, SpO2, temperature) not obtained; comprehensive ROS (fever, hemoptysis, leg pain/swelling, syncope) not documented; detailed allergy reaction to ibuprofen not specified; medication dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Conflicts noted:
  - Date of birth stated by patient as 04/20/1980; clinician restated 1983 later in the conversation (conflict noted).
  - Pulse measurement: 30 beats counted over an unspecified interval; interpreted as slightly fast by clinician (interval not documented).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor incomplete/elliptical statements.
